norms.text: The watch is called on the hour, day and night.
The duty roster on the tree is kept current by the serjeant in his own hand.
The men at the barricade take the levy from every traveller.

taboos.text: Letting the colours touch the mud.
Selling Legion issue gear for food.

values.text: Kit kept in fighting order, though the men are hungry.
The pay book, with the column's last entry in it.

place.text: A level bench by a spring tarn, out of sight of the road. The column holds it as a posting.

work.text: The levy buys the food. The food runs short.

danger.text: Hackwings nest on the hill above; rats get into the meal sacks at night.

rumour.text: The governor at Gideon will not pay to clear the camp. The toll company's officers would use the men.

directions.text: Down the track to the Mile House, or to Cartwright's Cross, then the Gideon road.

addressTerms.text: Citizen, in the old Legion phrasing, to anyone on the track.

neverSaid.text: That the column deserted. The men say the column was left.

grievances.text: The Legion never paid the column for the months before the recall.

rumours.text: Gideon might offer a pardon and a wage.

views.text: Road folk who pay the levy and curse it down the hill.

dissent.text: A pardon without the back pay in the pay book is worth nothing to him; he parleys for the book (record questHooks.opportunity).
